question_text: According to the lecture, how is product development changing?
hint: Think about whether the change touches single tasks or the whole lifecycle.

options.option_text: It is automating isolated tasks one at a time while the overall lifecycle stays the same.
options.option_explanation: The lecture says product development is moving from isolated tasks to a reshaped lifecycle, so the lifecycle itself changes.

options.option_text: It is narrowing its focus to regulatory compliance and leaving ideation behind.
options.option_explanation: The transformation covers the whole span, from the "fuzzy front end" of ideation to regulatory compliance.

options.option_text: It is moving from isolated tasks to a reshaped lifecycle.
options.option_explanation: Correct. Product development is undergoing a fundamental transformation, moving from isolated tasks to a reshaped lifecycle.

options.option_text: It is making small refinements to existing tools rather than a fundamental change.
options.option_explanation: The lecture describes a fundamental transformation, not small refinements.

question_text: According to the lecture, which kind of ideas are LLMs better at generating?
hint: The lecture contrasts incremental ideas with paradigm shifts.

options.option_text: Big ideas that set off paradigm shifts, more than small incremental ones.
options.option_explanation: It is the reverse: LLMs are better at "small ideas" (incremental) than "big ideas" (paradigm shifts).

options.option_text: Small incremental ideas, more than big paradigm shifts.
options.option_explanation: Correct. LLMs are better at "small ideas" (incremental) than "big ideas" (paradigm shifts).

options.option_text: Ideas retrieved directly from existing information, never novel combinations.
options.option_explanation: The lecture describes LLMs as ideation engines that generate novel combinations rather than just retrieving information.

options.option_text: Big and small ideas equally well, because LLMs narrow the solution space.
options.option_explanation: LLMs excel at expanding the solution space, and they are better at small ideas than big ones.
